messages:
leo: quick flag from int8 bringup for lite-ranker-v1. ndcg@10 is within noise but MRR on the multilingual slice (es/ja/pt) fell ~0.03. curious if anyone's seen tokenizer-induced reorders before? :confused:
nina: hmm, tokenizer differences between our eval pipeline and the runtime can definitely flip short-title matches. did you run the same tokenizer version & vocab as serving?
leo: yes we pointed to bert-tokenizer v2 locally, but runtime uses sentencepiece v1.5 for the packed model. thinking mismatch. ran a token-count check and some queries truncate earlier under spm which changes context for priming.
jas: that would do it. truncated prefixes + quantized logits = unstable ordering. can you share per-query top5 before/after? small tie flips can kill MRR.
leo: pasted a small sample below (masked ids):
```
q1 (es): baseline fp16 top5 ids [A,B,C,D,E] scores [1.23,1.20,1.19,1.18,1.10]
q1 int8 top5 ids     [B,A,C,D,E] scores [1.22,1.21,1.18,1.17,1.09]
q7 (ja): baseline [X,Y,Z] scores [0.92,0.91,0.85]
q7 int8    [Y,X,Z] scores [0.90,0.89,0.84]
```
nina: classic near-tie flips. two action areas: 1) canonicalize tokenizer across eval/serving (use a shared tokenizer bundle in model package) 2) ensure prefix/priming padding is consistent (pad to same token length before priming). also add a deterministic post-sort tiebreaker by stable_docid.
jas: agree. add a small per-slice paired A/B test that reports fraction of queries with top1 changed and mean score delta for those. threshold the bringup to fail if >2% top1 flips for multilingual slice.
leo: running a quick retest with unified tokenizer bundle (spm v1.5) and fixed padding. command: `./eval/run.sh --model lite-ranker-v1 --quant int8 --slice multilingual --seed 7 --tokenizer spm-v1.5`
ci-bot: triggered run 1809998889 on runner-3 (multilang smoke) :gear:
ops: also check candidate dedupe/normalization. we had a case where accents/diacritics normalized differently causing duplicates that affect ranking ties. we should normalize canonical titles in preproc.
nina: good catch. add unicode normalization (NFC) and strip soft-hyphens before dedupe. small script: `python -c "import unicodedata; print(unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s))"`
leo: quick results: after tokenizer unification and padding, mrr delta reduced to 0.007 and top1-flip rate down to 0.9% on 5k queries. still non-zero but within threshold.
jas: nice. next steps: - open PR to include tokenizer bundle in model artifact - add padding normalization step in eval harness - implement stable tiebreaker in postprocess - add paired-top1 metric to bringup checks
leo: opening PRs now, will tag reviewers. also adding an entry to model-catalog: "lite-ranker-v1 int8: prefers shared spm-v1.5 tokenizer; consider padding to min 16 tokens for primed queries"
ci-bot: created ticket #ML-2207 for multilingual top1 flip alerting and linked this thread.
ops: long-term, let's add a small randomized seeding check across hardware (cpu vs gpu host kernels) because non-determinism in kernels + quantization can show up only on certain hosts.
leo: agreed. thanks all — filing follow-up tests and will re-run full bringup after PR merge.
